items.stem:
Gupta and Sons prepared a detailed three-year plan for its textbooks business in Guwahati. Midway, a new competitor cut prices, but the managers kept following the original plan and lost market share.

items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Planning leads to rigidity; planning may not work in a dynamic environment. (ii) Reviewed the premises and revised the plan (planning is continuous and must be flexible).

items.stem: Reddy Enterprises prepares a detailed plan for launching a new product, with tasks, schedules, resources and costs. Which type of plan is this?
items.answer: Programme
items.markingKey: (b) Programme. A detailed plan for a project.
options: Method
Programme
Procedure
Rule

items.stem: Explain the following points of importance of planning: (i) Planning establishes standards for controlling (ii) Planning provides direction.
items.answer: (i) Planning establishes standards for controlling: It gives the goals against which performance is measured. (ii) Planning provides direction: It states in advance how work is to be done.
items.markingKey: 2 marks each: (i) It gives the goals against which performance is measured. (ii) It states in advance how work is to be done.

items.stem:
Harpreet, the owner of Sethi Brothers, started a new textbooks line without setting targets or studying alternatives. After launch he never checked progress. Sales were poor.
(i) Which steps of planning did Harpreet skip? (ii) Explain how any two of them would have helped.
items.answer: (i) Setting objectives; developing premises; identifying and evaluating alternatives; follow-up action. (ii) Objectives give direction; evaluating alternatives selects the best course; follow-up corrects deviations in time.
items.markingKey: 6 marks: (i) Setting objectives; developing premises; identifying and evaluating alternatives; follow-up action. (ii) Objectives give direction; evaluating alternatives selects the best course; follow-up corrects deviations in time.

items.stem: Which of the following best describes "Procedure"?
items.answer: The routine steps on how to carry out an activity, in chronological order.
items.markingKey: (d) Procedure: The routine steps on how to carry out an activity, in chronological order.
options: A statement of expected results expressed in numerical terms.
A plan used repeatedly for situations that occur again and again, such as policies, procedures, methods and rules.
A plan developed for a one-time event or project, such as a programme or budget.
The routine steps on how to carry out an activity, in chronological order.

items.stem: At Kulkarni Industries, a purchase request must be approved by the department head, then by finance, before an order is placed. Which type of plan is this? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Procedure. Routine steps in chronological order.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Procedure; 2 marks for the justification: Routine steps in chronological order.

items.stem: State one difference between policy and rule on the basis of penalty.
items.answer: policy: no penalty for deviation; rule: violation attracts a penalty
items.markingKey: 1 mark: policy: no penalty for deviation; rule: violation attracts a penalty

items.stem: Menon Industries kept extra stock of raw material because its plan expected a transport strike. Which importance, feature or limitation of planning is highlighted? Justify your answer.
items.answer: Planning reduces the risks of uncertainty. Managers anticipate changes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark for identifying Planning reduces the risks of uncertainty; 2 marks for the justification: Managers anticipate changes.

items.stem: Which of the following statements about types of plans is correct?
items.answer: A budget is a plan expressed in numbers.
items.markingKey: (d) Correct: A budget is a plan expressed in numbers.
options: Objectives are the routine steps for an activity.
A rule is a general guideline.
A policy allows no discretion at all.
A budget is a plan expressed in numbers.

items.stem:
Reddy Retail wants to double the sales of textbooks in Kochi. Its managers assumed that demand would grow by 10%, listed three ways to grow, compared their costs and returns, and chose franchising.
(i) Identify the steps of planning covered so far. (ii) Name the two steps that remain and explain one.
items.answer: (i) Setting objectives; developing premises; identifying alternatives; evaluating alternatives; selecting an alternative. (ii) Implementing the plan and follow-up action; follow-up checks that the plan is carried out and corrects deviations.
items.markingKey: 4 marks: (i) Setting objectives; developing premises; identifying alternatives; evaluating alternatives; selecting an alternative. (ii) Implementing the plan and follow-up action; follow-up checks that the plan is carried out and corrects deviations.

items.stem: Ahuja Stores checks every month whether online sales are on target. Which step of the planning process is described?
items.answer: Follow-up action
items.markingKey: (c) Follow-up action. The plan is monitored.
options: Setting objectives
Implementing the plan
Follow-up action
Identifying alternative courses of action

items.stem: Distinguish between single-use plans and standing plans on the basis of meaning, examples and duration.
items.answer: (i) Meaning: single-use plans: developed for a one-time event or project; standing plans: used repeatedly for recurring situations. (ii) Examples: single-use plans: programmes and budgets; standing plans: policies, procedures, methods and rules. (iii) Duration: single-use plans: for a specific period or project; standing plans: for a longer period.

items.stem: What is meant by "Alternative courses of action"?
items.answer: The different ways in which an objective may be achieved, identified during planning.
